route.ask: Which one does the request ask for?

errors.what:
Show the error rate of a service.
The share of its requests failing over the last hour and when it rose, in one region or all.
not_for: the error messages in a service's logs
a service that is down or broken
examples: error rate of payments in eu-west
how many checkout requests are erroring
show me the 5xx on search in us-east
what is the error rate of checkout
is search failing in us east

deploys.what:
List the recent deploys of a service.
Each release with when it went out and who shipped it, in one region or all.
examples: what got deployed to checkout recently
recent releases of search in us-east
who shipped to payments in eu-west
show the deploys of search in us east

logs.what:
Search a service's logs from the last hour.
Its most frequent error messages and how often each came, in one region or all.
not_for: a service's deploy log or release history
examples: search the payments logs in eu-west
what do the search logs say
what is checkout logging in us-east
what errors are in the payments logs in eu west

suspect.what:
Find the release most likely behind a failure.
Weighs the errors, deploys and logs found before it in the same request, and names one release.
examples: find the release behind the outage

rollback.what:
Roll a service back from a release to the one before it.
Everywhere or in one region; live traffic moves to the older release, and only a new deploy brings the newer one back.
not_for: a config change or a feature flag
examples: back out 5.4.1 on checkout in us-east
roll back the last payments deploy

post.what:
Post a message to a chat channel.
To one of your team's chat channels; the message is the words that asked for it.
not_for: a direct message to one person
examples: post to #incident that we are on it
drop a line in #ops about payments
write in the incident channel that we are on it

incidents.what:
List the open incidents.
Each with its number and the service it hit; closed ones are left out.
not_for: looking up one incident by its number

incident.what:
Look up an incident by its number.
What happened, when it opened and which service it hit.

postmortem.what:
Draft the postmortem of an incident.
Written from the incident looked up before it in the same request, and saved as a draft for review.
not_for: looking up what happened in an incident
posting a summary to a channel

status.what:
Update the status page for a service.
What customers see until the next update: investigating, identified, monitoring or resolved; monitoring when none is named.
not_for: asking how a service is doing
examples: update the status page for checkout
mark payments as resolved on the status page
set the search status to investigating
show checkout as identified on the status page
put payments in monitoring on the status page
tell customers we are monitoring search
